checks: Original 3787afd8b1ed0167 §§1–3 gives the same ordinary global statement and TV consequence by maximum-inscribed normalization and a fixed positive depth gap. Original e2c21ddfc5abb8ca §3 (9)–(11a) gives the same enclosure-volume factor, absolute defect budget, retained Q-minus-K slack and scale-aware bound. The frozen proof preserves these scopes and uses a dimension-only threshold from the accepted compact normalization.

An enclosing simplex exists by boundedness of Q. An inball of Q gives a fixed positive equatorial disk for each nonzero vertex direction. Its cone belongs to each enclosing simplex, so a uniform volume bound bounds all vertices. Convex hulls of convergent tuples converge in Hausdorff distance and the determinant is continuous. The limit contains the full-dimensional Q and is a simplex. A facet with positive separation from Q can move inward slightly and strictly reduce volume.

For maximum-volume inscribed T, replacing a vertex by x has determinant magnitude |λ_j(x)| times the old one, so |λ_j(x)|≤1. The outer set defined by λ_j≥−1 is exactly a translate of (d+2)T, since the shifted barycentric coordinates sum to d+2. The determinant volume factor is (d+2)^d, and T⊂Q gives the required universal bound.

Euclidean Hausdorff closeness from 03bc771bddd39a8a implies the required infinity-norm closeness. The cutoff ε≤1/(64d³) implies both locality thresholds in e823c82617a0bc70. That result works for every minimum enclosure and gives both the vertex match and each actual facet-centroid contact. Averaging the matched vertices gives ||g_S−g_T||∞≤Lε. The barycentric defining inequalities of T give the inradius ρ=1/[d(d+1)] about g_T in the infinity norm. The chosen δ=2Lε/ρ≤δ_d also ensures Lε≤ρ/2.

For each direction the Hausdorff bound yields h_S−h_Q≤Lε||u||₁, because Q contains T. The translated infinity ball in S gives h_S−u·g_S≥(ρ/2)||u||₁. Hence the support of g_S+(1−δ)(S−g_S) is h_S−δ(h_S−u·g_S)≤h_Q. This is exactly the inner inclusion in c99394a395ea2399. Dividing its gain by Γ_dc/4 produces the local factor, and above the fixed cutoff the ratio defect ≤1 gives the global factor 1/(Γ_dτ). Both constants depend only on d.

An invertible affine map sends minimum enclosing simplices to minimum enclosing simplices, preserves normalized halfspace depth and changes numerator and denominator volumes by a common determinant. The nested uniform densities have positive difference only on Q, whose positive mass is 1−|Q|/|S|. The usual TV supremum therefore bounds every closed-halfspace probability difference.

The frozen transfer uses the same normals and all finitely many nonnegative weights. It proves K⊂R⊂S for R=Σλ_iP_i and retains the exact slack |S|−|K|=(|S|−|Q|)+(|Q|−|K|). Multiplying the ordinary bound by |S| and applying the upper volume estimate gives the stated coefficient A_d(d+2)^d|Q|. When Q=K, actual facet contact gives R=S, so division by |S| gives λ_i^d|P_i|/|S|=α_i^d. Zero weights and translated summands are allowed, and in dimension one the two support bounds recover each input interval exactly.

The centroid and scale identities were checked algebraically, including the common determinant factor and the positive denominator Σλ_i r_i. An independent rational replay for d=2 through 32 also checked the locality inequalities, positivity of the local coefficient and the normalized powers with a zero weight and weights not summing to one.
Linked independent recheck verified the unchanged proof against the exact revised parallel-simplex enclosure theorem.

overlap.comparison: In every d≥3 it gives the same enclosure defect bound using paired depth P(Q). At each y, setting the paired offset to s=0 gives p_Q(y)≤ordinary depth at y, hence P(Q)≤D(Q). This implies the ordinary bound for every minimum enclosure in d≥3, including TV by the nested-density identity. The frozen proof additionally treats d=2 and supplies the Minkowski defect budgets.

It already provides the local linear depth bound and TV equality under inner homothetic containment and every facet-centroid contact. The present proof supplies these hypotheses uniformly near equality in an inscribed normalization and adds the far-body and Minkowski bounds.
